brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Two storeys of bases with top covers (cover:-1,0,1, cover:0,0,1, cover:1,0,1) make the shelf. A row of books and a stack of books sit on it with no prop warnings.
drawer:0#-1,0#cut and drawer:0#1,0#cut sit in the cut faces of the two half bases on the bottom storey.
The configurator only checks fit and collisions, not strength or load. The parts are 3D printed in whatever material you choose, and nothing here can show whether the unit holds 50 kg.

finish.summary: I built a two-storey shelf unit with two drawers and the books on top, but I can't confirm it will hold 50 kg. The bottom storey is a full base with a south-half base on each side. Each half base holds a drawer in its cut face (drawer:0#-1,0#cut and drawer:0#1,0#cut). The second storey has the same layout. Covers on top make the shelf surface, which holds a row of books and a stack of books. Every open face is capped and the joints are bolted. check_build shows no issues and the mesh-collision check reads clear. The unit is 53 parts and an estimated 2,527 g of filament.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
